t: Concept Clustering Engine: a plain-language overview
title: Concept Clustering Engine: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Concept Clustering Engine does and why archives need it. A concept clustering engine looks at a mountain of records and sorts them into piles that belong together — all the astronomy articles in one pile, all the cooking articles in another. It decides what belongs together by the words the records use. Nobody labels anything by hand; the piles emerge from the data.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Concept Clustering Engine works
title: How the Concept Clustering Engine works
description: Overview: what the Concept Clustering Engine does and why archives need it. Real clustering turns documents into TF-IDF vectors or dense embeddings, then groups them with k-means, agglomerative clustering, or HDBSCAN, which also finds outliers that belong to no pile. Each cluster gets an automatic label from its most distinctive terms (top TF-IDF words or a centroid-nearest phrase), and quality is scored with silhouette coefficients or coherence metrics. The result is a set of labeled groups with membership lists and per-document assignment confidence.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Concept Clustering Engine works: the deep tour
title: How the Concept Clustering Engine works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Concept Clustering Engine does and why archives need it. Real clustering turns documents into TF-IDF vectors or dense embeddings, then groups them with k-means, agglomerative clustering, or HDBSCAN, which also finds outliers that belong to no pile. Each cluster gets an automatic label from its most distinctive terms (top TF-IDF words or a centroid-nearest phrase), and quality is scored with silhouette coefficients or coherence metrics. The result is a set of labeled groups with membership lists and per-document assignment confidence. Advanced engines choose the cluster count with elbow or gap statistics, handle hierarchical topics with multi-level clustering, and re-cluster incrementally as new records arrive without reshuffling everything. Quality is checked against human-labeled samples with adjusted Rand index. The limits are genuinely mixed documents that belong to several topics — assigned to the best fit with secondary memberships recorded — and tiny clusters that may be noise, which the engine reports with their size rather than hiding them.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
